reason: The goal is to push a wheel onto a straw, so I'll start with the first of each.

reason: I'll add the next wheel to the axle, matching the current goal.

effect: The first wheel pair is attached, and the remaining pair is next.

effect: Both wheel pairs are attached, and the chassis now needs to be turned upright.

effect: The chassis is upright, and the remaining goal is to fit the sail.
reaction: The final assembly step is clear.
reason: The only offered combination joins the sail to the chassis, matching the goal.
expectation: I expect the sail to mount on the wheeled chassis, completing the racer.

effect: The sail and chassis became a wind racer, completing the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate assemblies become a finished racer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the sail to the wheeled chassis brought the construction together into a recognizable racer.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the second wheel pair repeated the first assembly, though it was clear why it was needed.

surprise.text: Nothing was particularly surprising; the goals made the sequence predictable.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the fittings and flip had clear roles in assembling the racer.

continue.text: I might continue for another hands-on build, though I would hope for a little more variety than the repeated wheel assembly.
